arguments.value: Football Northwest LLC agreed to give Mercata, Inc. a package of sponsorship, advertising, and promotional benefits connected to the Seattle Seahawks and the Kingdome in exchange for a $40,000 sponsorship fee. The benefits included preseason TV commercials and on-air mentions, stadium DiamondVision announcements and promotions, online advertising and store promotion on Seahawks.com, and VIP items such as tickets, a training camp trip, and ad space. The agreement started on July 19, 1999 and lasted until the promised benefits were completed, but not beyond the end of the 1999 season. Either side could terminate on 45 days’ notice if the Kingdome was closed for more than 30 days, the Seahawks franchise was cancelled or moved more than 50 miles from Seattle, or the other party materially breached and failed to cure within 30 days. The agreement says Washington law governs, with exclusive venue in King County Superior Court or the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, and disputes may be arbitrated under AAA rules in Seattle. Each party kept its own trademark rights, the sponsor’s creative materials were subject to objection by FNW, both sides had indemnity obligations, the agreement was confidential, and assignment was restricted.
